headline: Revenue grows, impairment sinks earnings, guidance raised
summary_short: Americold's Q2 FY2026 revenue rose 1.9% y/y to $662.9 million, but a $309.6 million impairment tied to exiting two facilities drove a net loss of $342.8 million ($1.19 per diluted share), versus net income a year ago.
summary_long: Revenue rose 1.9% y/y to $662.9M on higher transportation revenue, same-store rate gains, and favorable FX, partly offset by lost non-same-store revenue from site exits. Same-store NOI fell 1.5% y/y as higher power and labor costs outpaced rate gains; services margin slipped to 14.8% from 15.2%. Net loss of $342.8M ($1.19/diluted share) reflects a $309.6M impairment tied to winding down the Lancaster, PA and Plainville, CT sites, plus higher depreciation and a smaller real-estate gain. Adjusted FFO was $0.35/share, down 2.8% y/y. Cash fell to $40.5M from $101.4M a year ago after $200M of note repayments and $132.6M of distributions. Full-year Adjusted FFO guidance raised to $1.26-$1.32/share, more than offsetting projected EQT joint-venture dilution.

drivers.explanation: Rose on higher transportation-services revenue, same-store rate increases, and favorable FX, partly offset by lost non-same-store revenue from portfolio-management site exits.
Swing to a $342.8M net loss was principally driven by a $309.6M impairment tied to exiting the Lancaster, PA and Plainville, CT facilities, plus higher D&A and a smaller real-estate gain.
Turned negative as the $309.6M impairment charge and higher transactions/strategic-initiative costs outweighed underlying segment NOI.
Moved to a $1.19 per-share loss from $0.01 income a year ago, tracking the net-loss swing on a roughly flat diluted share count.
Fell to $40.5M as $200M of senior-note repayment and $132.6M of distributions in financing activities outpaced $232.5M of new term-loan proceeds.
Declined y/y as the net loss (chiefly the impairment) widened the accumulated deficit, partly offset by ongoing paid-in-capital growth.

Raised full-year Adjusted FFO guidance to $1.26-$1.32/share (from $1.20-$1.30 ex-JV as of Feb 19, 2026), saying the improved outlook more than offsets projected dilution from the pending EQT joint venture.
